record.name: Kunlu Mountain Imperial Tribute Sheng Cha

paragraphs.text: [Kunlu Mountain](kunlu-mountain:where) is a spur of the Wuliang range in Ning’er County, Pu’er City, with heights given at about 1,410 to 2,271 metres. Its [old tea trees](kunlu-mountain:trees) cover a little over 10,000 mu. They stand tall and mostly unpruned, with wild, transitional and planted types growing side by side, and the trade knows the mountain for them.

This is [raw pu’er](sheng:identity) from 2007. It was never given shou’s fast fermentation, so its character changes slowly over years. Raw pu’er is wok fired and then sun dried into [maocha](sheng:making), and this tea was left loose rather than pressed into a cake.

At nineteen years it has had almost two decades of [change in storage](sheng:aging), and it sits on the line the trade still argues over. Some call raw pu’er [aged](sheng:ageing) after ten years, and many wait for twenty or more.

brewing.text: Young raw pu’er takes water a little off the boil, about 85 to 95°C, because hotter water draws out more of its bitterness; an aged one takes 95°C to boiling. A common start is about 7 grams to 100 ml and a quick rinse of a few seconds, then a first steep of ten to fifteen seconds, adding a few seconds each round. A good raw tea gives eight to ten cups or more.

notice.text: A smoother, thicker, sweeter cup with woody, herbal and camphor notes and something of dried dates or dark fruit.
